summaryAnalyses.title: What each visitor kind understood, and what they would do next
summaryAnalyses.instruction: For each visitor kind, write 2-3 sentences: what these personas concluded the company or product does and for whom (note where they got it wrong or stayed vague), whether the first screen kept them reading and what decided it, which of their own problems they recognised, and what they would do next and why. Keep the case where someone understood and valued the offer but was not ready to make contact, and say what they would need first. Mark wording quoted from the page as quoted; everything else is persona interpretation. Do not invent.

summaryAnalyses.title: Findings: what creates confusion, doubt or hesitation, with exact wording
summaryAnalyses.instruction: For each visitor kind, cluster what these personas found confusing, missing, unconvincing or irrelevant into at most four findings, most frequent first. For each finding give: the exact section or wording (keep the [position/kind] tag and quote wording exactly as written), who it affects, and what it creates (confusion, doubt, hesitation). Then list the claims these personas would not accept without proof, quoted, with the kind of proof they wanted. Quoted wording is what is visible on the site; everything else is persona interpretation - label them. Do not invent findings.

summaryAnalyses.title: The primary button: expectation vs what followed
summaryAnalyses.instruction: For each visitor kind, describe in 2-3 sentences what these personas expected the button to lead to, what they actually found after clicking - what the page or form asks for - and where reality fell short of or exceeded the expectation. Report only what the personas observed; where a persona did not inspect the button, say it is unknown. Do not invent.

summaryAnalyses.title: What to change, how to check it, and what to keep
summaryAnalyses.instruction: For each visitor kind, cluster the suggested changes into at most four concrete themes, most frequent first. For each theme give a short imperative title, one representative verbatim quote, and how the site owner could tell whether the change helped (use the personas' own checks). Then, in one or two sentences, what these personas said already works and should be kept, naming the elements. These are instructions to the website owner: specific and actionable. Do not invent suggestions that were not made.
